evidence.evidence_text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), by incorporating external knowledge with parametric memory of language models, has become the state-of-the-art architecture for open-domain QA tasks.
In this paper, we propose an Induction-Augmented Generation (IAG) framework that utilizes inductive knowledge along with the retrieved documents for implicit reasoning.
We leverage large language models (LLMs) for deriving such knowledge via a novel prompting method based on inductive reasoning patterns.

IAG-GPT directly utilizes the knowledge generated by GPT-3 for answer prediction, while IAG-Student gets rid of dependencies on GPT service at inference time by incorporating a student inductor model.

IAG-GPT directly utilizes the knowledge generated by GPT-3 for answer prediction, while IAG-Student gets rid of dependencies on GPT service at inference time by incorporating a student inductor model.
The inductor is firstly trained via knowledge distillation and further optimized by back-propagating the generator feedback via differentiable beam scores.
Notably, our best models have won the first place in the official leaderboards of CSQA2.0 (since Nov 1, 2022) and StrategyQA (since Jan 8, 2023).

The inductor is firstly trained via knowledge distillation and further optimized by back-propagating the generator feedback via differentiable beam scores.
